stem: Pihu keeps a sprouting seed and a green leaf overnight in a dark cupboard. She asks what happens when these living plant parts respire to release energy.

statements.text: In living plant parts, glucose reacts with oxygen to release carbon dioxide, water, and energy.
Only green parts carry out respiration; non-green parts such as roots do not.
Glucose reacts with nitrogen instead of oxygen in every plant part during respiration.

teacher.key_rationale: Respiration uses glucose and oxygen in all living plant parts, releasing CO2, water, and energy. Non-green parts also respire, and nitrogen does not replace oxygen in that reaction.
